question: were the span elision and pointer retention paths switched off by configuration, or did they simply never trigger?
answer: neither: those paths are not wired into the chain at all. The plugin arm in every recent batch is the frozen v12 exact duplicate rule and nothing else, and the only counter that moves is the one that counts duplicate replacements

decisions_this_settles.c_duplicate_dose_is_now_near_tautologica: measuring how the saving varies with the amount of duplication would re-measure a rule whose definition is 'replace byte identical duplicates'; it would add no decision value, and its only practical use would be to raise the headline figure by adding duplicates, which the mechanism correction explicitly forbids
decisions_this_settles.the_real_headroom_is_d: the only way to obtain saving on content that does not repeat is to wire one of the earlier mechanisms - selective retention with the literal guard, or span and pointer retention - into the chain as a new host configuration, and then measure it on the same fixed tasks and the same shape against the same baseline arm
decisions_this_settles.what_d_must_prove: that it compresses unique content at all, and that the strict track stays at or above the baseline while it does; the earlier versions were probed on single axis pilots, so neither property is established at the three task, three arm scale
decisions_this_settles.what_d_must_not_do: it may not reuse the v16 sealed tasks, may not merge its percentages with any earlier batch, and may not be run without pinning every module hash in its freeze and exercising the finalisation path inside the zero API gate
